answer: A network can resist Sybil attacks by tying each identity's weight to the smaller of two independent costs: verifiable work and locked stake. Like a comet that only shines when ice and sunlight meet, an identity gains influence only where proof of work and escrowed funds overlap. Through this inlet, cheap clones pass neither gate: stake without work, or compute without stake, yields zero weight. Influence grows like a vine only where both roots run deep, so forging a thousand fake agents means paying a thousand work proofs and a thousand locked deposits, while an honest agent pays once.
